entities.summary: Carlo Ruzzini was a Venetian diplomat and statesman who served as the doge of Venice from 1732 to 1735. A member of the aristocratic family of Ruzzini, he was born into a prominent Venetian family and received a classical education. Ruzzini's diplomatic career spanned several continents, including his service as an envoy to the Holy Roman Empire and the Ottoman Empire. He played a key role in negotiating the Treaty of Passarowitz, which ended the War of the Polish Succession. Ruzzini's leadership and diplomacy were instrumental in maintaining Venice's independence during a period of significant turmoil in Europe. He died on January 5, 1735, at the age of 64, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most important figures in Venetian history. The city of Venice continued to thrive under his successors, who continued to navigate the complexities of European politics. Ruzzini's contributions to the field of diplomacy and his role in shaping the future of Venice remain an important part of the city's history. The legacy of Carlo Ruzzini serves as a testament to the enduring power of diplomacy and leadership in shaping the course of human history.
